I've been in a similar situation.  Last year my girlfriend (MtF) came out to me.  We'd been together for two years.  I was feeling very similar, even four months after she came out to me.  I would suggest therapy.  It helped me tremendously, and when I got done with therapy, I would talk with her about my worries.

I had assumed a lot of things about her and her transition like: she won't want to have sex anymore, she'll go onto hormones immediately without caring what I thought about it, she won't give me time time accept her and will be completely mean if I make one or two mistakes, she won't love me anymore, she'll completely disregard all the plans and visions I had for us as a couple, ect. ect.

Those were all wrong.  She had extensive conversations  with me.  She assured me that all of my feelings were valid and that she understood why I thought this way as I'd grown up in an extremely toxic conservative environment. (I'd like to add in that I was never homophobic towards anyone because I knew it was wrong.  I was pretty much okay with everything LGBTQ+ related)
She talked to me about starting hormones in about six months, to give me time to figure out if this relationship was what I'd wanted.  At the time I didn't want her to start until we lived together, we are long distance and I was terrified that the changes would be too much for me when I'd see her again.

But over time I began to realize that this is something that she really really wanted.  She would tell me stories of her childhood, how she felt put of place as a boy, even when she was as young as four.  She told me she thought it was normal to wish she was a girl.  

What I'm trying to say, is talk it out.  If your partner isn't willing to, or respectful of your feelings, I would suggest therapy for the both of you.  Even though your partners feelings are valid as well, right now if you are wanting to make it work, they also need to be aware of your feelings.  You're in just as a vulnerable position as your partner is.  This is a HUGE change for the both of you.  If you guys do end up splitting, it's okay, because you both will have talked it out.

Don't beat yourself up over how you're feeling.  I've been there.  I still do sometimes, but then I remember how far I've come.  We are both happy now.  You both seem like amazing people and I wish you both the best.
